title: The Necklace
author: Guy de Maupassant
summary: Em Paris, Mathilde Loisel é bonita e charmosa, mas vive uma vida simples com o marido, um funcionário modesto. Ela sonha com luxo, festas e vestidos caros. Quando um convite para um grande baile chega, ela pede emprestado um colar de diamantes a uma amiga rica, e uma noite perfeita pode mudar toda a sua vida.

chapters.title: A Woman Who Dreams
paragraphs: Mathilde is a young woman in Paris. She is pretty and charming. But her family is not rich. So she marries a small clerk. His name is Monsieur Loisel. He works at the Ministry of Education.
Mathilde is not happy. Her apartment is small and poor. The walls are old. The chairs are ugly. She has a little maid, but the maid makes her sad too. Mathilde thinks, “I am born for a better life.”
Every day she dreams. She dreams of big, quiet rooms with silk on the walls. She dreams of beautiful dinners with silver plates. She dreams of rich men who smile at her.
At dinner, her husband opens the soup. “Oh, good soup!” he says. “There is nothing better!” But Mathilde thinks of fine fish and expensive wine.
She has no jewels. She has no nice dresses. And she loves only those things. She wants people to admire her. She wants to be elegant.
She has one rich friend, Madame Forestier. They were at school together. But Mathilde does not like to visit her now. After every visit, she cries for days. She cries because she is poor.

chapters.title: The Invitation
paragraphs: One evening, Monsieur Loisel comes home with a big smile. He has a white envelope in his hand. “Look, Mathilde!” he says. “This is for you.”
She opens it. It is an invitation. The Minister of Education is giving a ball. Monsieur and Madame Loisel are invited.
Her husband thinks she is going to be happy. But she throws the card on the table. “What can I do with this?” she says.
“But, my dear, I work hard for this! Everybody wants to go. All the important people are going to be there.”
Mathilde looks at him with angry eyes. “And what can I wear?” she asks. Then she starts to cry.
He is surprised. “Your theatre dress is very pretty,” he says.
“No. I have nothing to wear. Give the card to a friend. Give it to a man with a rich wife.”
“How much is a good dress, Mathilde?”
She thinks for a moment. “About four hundred francs,” she says.

Her husband goes a little pale. He has exactly four hundred francs. It is his money for a new gun. He wants to go hunting with his friends in the summer. But he says, “All right. I can give you four hundred francs. Buy a beautiful dress.”
The day of the ball is near. The dress is ready. But Mathilde is sad again. “I have no jewels,” she says. “I look so poor.”
“Wear some flowers,” says her husband. “They are very fashionable.”
“No. There is nothing worse than looking poor among rich women.”
“Then go to your friend, Madame Forestier. Ask her for some jewels.”
Mathilde gives a cry of joy. “Yes! Of course!”

chapters.title: A Perfect Night
paragraphs: The next day, Mathilde visits Madame Forestier. She tells her the problem. Her friend opens a big box. “Choose something, my dear,” she says.
Mathilde sees bracelets and a necklace of pearls. She sees a gold cross with stones. She tries them on in front of the mirror. But she wants something more.
“Do you have anything else?” she asks.
“Yes, of course. Look in the boxes.”

Then she finds it. In a black box, there is a necklace of diamonds. It is wonderful. Her heart beats fast. Her hands shake. She puts it on her neck. She looks at herself in the mirror for a long time.
“Can I borrow this? Only this?” she asks.
“Yes, of course.”
Mathilde kisses her friend and runs home with her treasure.

The night of the ball arrives. Mathilde is the most beautiful woman there. She is elegant and smiling and full of joy. All the men look at her. They want to know her name. They all want to dance with her. Even the Minister notices her.
She dances and dances. She forgets everything. She is drunk with pleasure. This is the night of her dreams.
At four in the morning, they leave. Her husband puts her old coat on her shoulders. It is a poor coat. Mathilde feels ashamed. She runs down the steps quickly, so the rich women cannot see it.
They cannot find a cab. They walk to the river, cold and tired. At last they find an old cab. It takes them home.
At home, Mathilde stands in front of the mirror. She wants to see herself in her glory one more time. Then she gives a cry.
The necklace is not on her neck.

chapters.title: Ten Hard Years
paragraphs: “What is it?” asks her husband.
“The necklace! Madame Forestier's necklace! It is gone!”

They look in her dress, in her coat, in her pockets. Nothing. Her husband goes out again. He walks all the way back to the ball. He goes to the police and to the cab companies. He puts an advertisement in the newspapers. He finds nothing.
“We must write to your friend,” he says. “Tell her the clasp is broken. Tell her it is at the jeweller's. Then we have time.”

After a week, they have no hope. They go from shop to shop. At last, in a shop near the Palais Royal, they find a necklace of diamonds. It looks exactly the same. The price is forty thousand francs. The jeweller can sell it for thirty-six thousand.

Monsieur Loisel has eighteen thousand francs from his father. He borrows the rest. He borrows a thousand francs here, five hundred there. He signs many papers. He promises to pay back everything. He buys the necklace.
Mathilde takes it back to Madame Forestier. Her friend is a little cold. “You are late,” she says. “I need it.” She does not open the box. Mathilde is happy about that.

Now Mathilde knows the life of the very poor. She sends away the maid. They move to a small room under the roof. She washes the dishes and the clothes. She carries water up the stairs every morning. She argues with the shopkeepers over every cent. Her husband works in the evenings too. Sometimes he works all night.
This goes on for ten years. At the end of ten years, they pay back everything.

chapters.title: The Truth
paragraphs: Mathilde looks old now. She is a strong, hard woman, like all poor women. Her hair is messy. Her skirts are crooked. Her hands are red. She talks loudly and washes the floors with big buckets of water.
But sometimes, when her husband is at the office, she sits by the window. She thinks of that night long ago. She thinks of the ball. She was so beautiful then! She was so admired!
What if she still had that necklace? Who knows? Life is strange. A small thing can save you or ruin you.
One Sunday, Mathilde is walking in the Champs-Élysées. She sees a woman with a child. It is Madame Forestier! She is still young, still beautiful, still charming.
Mathilde feels emotional. Should she speak to her? Yes, of course. The debts are paid now. She can tell her everything. Why not?
“Good morning, Jeanne.”
Madame Forestier does not know her. She is surprised that this poor woman says her name. “But, madame, I don't know you. I think you are making a mistake.”
“No. I am Mathilde Loisel.”
Her friend gives a cry. “Oh, my poor Mathilde! You are so changed!”
“Yes. My life was very hard after that night. Many bad days. And all because of you!”
“Because of me? How?”
“Do you remember the diamond necklace? For the Minister's ball?”
“Yes. And?”
“Well, I lost it.”
“What? But you brought it back to me.”
“I brought you another one, exactly the same. And for ten years we paid for it. It is not easy for us. We have nothing. But now it is finished, and I am very glad.”
Madame Forestier stops walking. “You bought a diamond necklace to replace mine?”
“Yes. You didn't notice? They were exactly the same.” Mathilde smiles with proud, simple joy.
Madame Forestier takes both her hands. She is very moved. “Oh, my poor Mathilde! But my necklace was false! It was worth five hundred francs at the most!”
